+-- Explicit customer authority. Apply after 0010 and 0011. No inferred grants,
+-- owners, credentials or customer-data migration is performed by this schema.
+CREATE TABLE operator_memberships (
+  account_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES operator_accounts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
+  tenant TEXT NOT NULL,
+  role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('operator', 'admin')),
+  disabled INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (disabled IN (0, 1)),
+  removed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (removed IN (0, 1)),
+  revision TEXT NOT NULL,
+  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
+  PRIMARY KEY (account_id, tenant)
+);
+CREATE INDEX idx_operator_memberships_tenant ON operator_memberships(tenant, account_id);
+
+CREATE TABLE operator_service_credentials (
+  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
+  subject TEXT NOT NULL,
+  tenant TEXT NOT NULL,
+  role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('operator', 'admin')),
+  token_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
+  expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
+  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
+  created_by TEXT NOT NULL,
+  revoked_at INTEGER
+);
+CREATE INDEX idx_operator_services_tenant ON operator_service_credentials(tenant, created_at);
+
+-- Only trusted stamp maintenance inserts here, never an HTTP recovery endpoint.
+-- A stable operation/password commitment permits exact retry reconciliation.
+-- Inserting a duplicate cannot fire this AFTER INSERT trigger. Do not replace
+-- this with a BEFORE INSERT trigger or INSERT OR REPLACE.
+CREATE TABLE operator_recovery_requests (
+  operation_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
+  attempt_id TEXT NOT NULL,
+  target_scope TEXT NOT NULL,
+  account_id TEXT NOT NULL,
+  email TEXT NOT NULL,
+  expected_revision INTEGER NOT NULL,
+  password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
+  flags TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (flags = 'temporary-password+enable'),
+  at INTEGER NOT NULL
+);
+CREATE TRIGGER operator_recovery_apply AFTER INSERT ON operator_recovery_requests
+BEGIN
+  SELECT CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (
+    SELECT 1 FROM operator_accounts
+    WHERE id = NEW.account_id AND email = NEW.email AND updated_at = NEW.expected_revision
+  ) THEN RAISE(ABORT, 'Recovery target changed') END;
+  UPDATE operator_accounts SET password_hash = NEW.password_hash,
+    must_change_password = 1, disabled = 0, updated_at = MAX(updated_at + 1, NEW.at)
+    WHERE id = NEW.account_id AND email = NEW.email AND updated_at = NEW.expected_revision;
+  DELETE FROM operator_sessions WHERE account_id = NEW.account_id;
+  INSERT INTO operator_audit (at, action, actor_id, target_id, target_email, detail)
+    VALUES (NEW.at, 'account_reset', 'stamp-maintenance', NEW.account_id, NEW.email,
+      json_object('operation', 'owner_recovery', 'operationId', NEW.operation_id));
+END;

 Sign-in, password replacement and account changes conditionally commit against the current account state. A concurrent account or session change returns `409` without new credentials; sign in again and retry with the current state. Password replacement installs its session and revokes the previous sessions atomically. Role or enabled-state changes end existing sessions and require a new sign-in. An existing account is never overwritten by legacy migration. Migration creates the account before committing the first session, so a failed session commit can leave a recoverable D1 account. Removal atomically deletes the account and its sessions and retains the actor-bearing removal audit. That retained record blocks legacy import by account ID or email, including an import already in flight, even if best-effort KV cleanup fails. An authorized admin can explicitly recreate a removed email with a new account ID and temporary password; this preserves the old removal barrier and requires normal password-change onboarding. Protection depends on retaining removal audit records and cannot reconstruct missing historical records. A lost response or failure of another audit write after a successful commit does not undo that commit.
 
 Every login mode requires admission before reading credentials or account stores: at most 100 admitted requests per stamp and 10 per source in each fixed 60-second window. `429` includes `Retry-After` in seconds and `X-RateLimit-Reset` as Unix milliseconds. Denied attempts do not extend that window. Only Cloudflare's `CF-Connecting-IP` selects a source; missing or invalid values share one budget. Its purpose-separated HMAC digest expires with the window; raw addresses, emails and tenant selectors are not stored in this limiter. This assumes trusted Cloudflare ingress. Shared networks and stamp-wide exhaustion can temporarily prevent login, but an attacker no longer locks an account by its email. Existing refresh, logout and password recovery remain outside the login budget. Unknown accounts perform a dummy password derivation and are always rejected; no constant-time or deployed capacity guarantee is implied.
 
-The shared tooling helper mints expiring `type: service` credentials. These retain explicit tenant grants and signed machine authority without human account/session lookup; human logout does not revoke them. Explicitly supplied tokens pass through unchanged. With exact `AUTH_MODE=enforced`, old untyped access tokens must be refreshed or replaced by signing in, and old machine tokens must be reminted. Unknown token types are refused in every mode. Non-enforced demo mode retains legacy untyped API compatibility and its revocation limitation. Global account administration remains unavailable in enforced mode pending tenant-scoped authority.
